set.body:
OPPORTUNITY rather than a defect. The comparative review surfaced a pedagogical device in rMVPA that effectagram could adopt almost verbatim, because effectagram already has the same structure and simply never names it.

rMVPA.Rmd:197-210 states four scientific objects and gives each a question:

  'the imaging measurements live in a dataset, the response and grouping variables
   live in a design, the estimator and resampling rule live in a model specification,
   and an engine decides WHERE to fit it'

  What are the measurements?                        -> mvpa_dataset
  What is predicted, what defines independence?     -> mvpa_design
  What is fitted and resampled?                     -> mvpa_model
  Where is it fitted?                               -> run_regional / run_searchlight

README.md:24-33 repeats it as an ASCII pipeline. The effect is that a reader holds four
nouns and four questions before touching any code, and every later function has a slot
to land in.

effectagram has exactly four objects in its main path and never presents them this way:

  What was measured, and in what independent pieces?   relation()
  Where in space is it summarized?                     compile_frame() + searchlights()/
                                                       voxels()/regions()/whole_brain()
  Which pieces must agree for the estimate to count?   cross_partitions()
  What question is asked of the result?                contrast()/rdm()/rsa()/
                                                       geometry_spectrum()

That is a genuinely clean decomposition and it is arguably CLEARER than rMVPA's, because
the third slot - which independent pieces must agree - is the scientific commitment this
package is actually built around, and it gets its own named object rather than hiding
inside a cross-validation argument. This is the framework's real pedagogical asset and
the docs currently spend it on nothing.

Contrast with what introduction.Rmd:29 does instead: its first heading is 'Declare the
native relation', which is slot one presented as a construction chore, with no map showing
that three more slots are coming or why.

PROPOSED: open both README and introduction.Rmd with the four questions, in question form,
before any code. Then let each section fill one slot. Costs nothing structural, touches no
semantics, and is the single highest-leverage prose change I can see.

Flagging one risk for claude-review: naming cross_partitions() as 'which pieces must agree'
is an interpretive gloss. It is accurate for the cross-run case the docs lead with, but the
object is more general than that gloss, and a reader who internalizes the gloss may be
surprised by the unequal-axis and bridge cases later in the same vignette. A frame that
teaches the common case fast at the cost of a later correction may still be the right trade,
but it IS a trade and should be made deliberately rather than by accident.
set.title: Adopt a four-object onboarding frame: the package already has one and never states it
